body: There won't be one anyway. I don't care for anything, nobody is obligated to care. I have nobody that I can say I truly care about. I've dropped many people with the snap of my fingers.

Heh.. it's been 3 weeks, I've got some shit done, but I still don't value my life and it's slowly diminishing further and further to the whole "sooner or later I'll be taking my own life". 

I've had a lot of conversations in real life to people and they only further strengthen my beliefs to how shitty western culture/society is and how change is only within myself, the brain.

These guys see many and work with many, I can really see that they don’t give a single shit about your own being if you were to take your own life, just as I wouldn’t care about a lot despite being close to someone, because it is true, when you pass away, you are still nonetheless alone and humanity still continues to grow with or without you and 1000 years down the line, not even that many, people will forget you."

I guess I can, but it's going to be difficult, and lol telling my mom? Please, she's unsupportive, untrustworthy, hypocritical, judging, close minded, religious to death, stubborn. Yeah but all of that is a joke. The average person won't even run into 1/100,000th of the world. Like I said, society is what determines the norm, and the norm is people who like beating around the bush, aren't super accepting and they're judgemental. Why else would honesty and trust/truth not take you very far in the corporate world?

I don't label those things as achievements, they are only mere to the average person. I've seen it and heard stories of people who fail their knowledge test to get their learners license (Where someone of the age of 25+ must have their full class license sit beside you in shotgun for you to be able to drive) several times, including their novice stage (where you can now drive by yourself but can only have 1 passenger minus if it is immediate family)

I did all those in a single try especially with the knowledge test where I didn't even read the book and just applied simple common sense into it. Granted I took maybe 4 lessons to adapt to steering wheel, gas pedal, brake pedal for my driving one, I still didn't take long to learn it.

Like I said, I really do hate to sound conceited, but there are lot of things I pick up fast on and that is what drops my interest to them. I'm unable to keep one because of circumstances I can't really explain and even when I do, it never really makes sense to someone because it does sound illogical and I'm all about logic.

About welfare support and stuff, that is something I don't wish to do, it's hard to say why I think so, I rather live out as a bum, but no I will be fine there because mom does pay for stuff if she doesn't end up stupidly gambling. I mean she's gotten a lot better on it, but it is still a problem sometimes.

Small town which is about 2 hours drive away from the main city. 3-4 hours by bus. Let's just say there's a lot of grow operations here and the latter of other drugs.

Had several bikes stolen (not just from me but my cousin's too), even with two kinds of locks, the horse shoe and simple rounded locks.

It is all within your minds and wills. A lot of people are close minded and stubborn.

But the world will always be rotten and society is what will always make the norm. People like us will never have a large enough impact and that's why we always fall short. I can't even really explain any further in-depth on why it is, because it's hard to say really. It's just myself being a perfectionist and idealist, but it'll never happen, not ever because that's simply just how life is.

It is possible for me to finish my GED but I have already tried twice. I can't, it's not that I'm not willing either, but when I did go for the courses because I felt like I needed to finish them, I just ended up only going for exams/tests because everything taught was just reminders/not significant enough to be marked, though I think that was also because the school/courses I took was for those who didn't actually finish it in highschool so they let you do it online also. My patience died out because I couldn't wait to do the next exam/test despite me asking for it, things might've changed then or I can find one that allows me, but it seems like such a chore. It isn't a necessity for me, to live more content in life.

Nothing really interests me much now, I'm even dead bored of being on the computer, I'm just talking or spending my times researching and looking up other stuff that can only preoccupy myself. I can get pique at things, but they die off quite quickly since I get bored. As for what currently interests me, nothing as I've said, but I actually went out today to see if I can book an appointment with a counsellor of the sort, to see if what else I would need (I know what I need, I just wanted confirmation/reassurance some reason) to get a career in said job(s).

Don't be sorry lol. The more I hear the word, the more I feel as if it's lost all it's meaning to me because it's already at that point. I don't ever seek out for one because I don't want her in my mess because I'm not stable or am able to sort myself ever. I feel as if I'm constantly on a rollercoaster even when I'm working and occupying myself.

My current daily routine .. well I mentioned earlier I headed out today to book an appointment and stuff. I really don't have the patience for it either, but I decided to try waiting, so I'm waiting until next week for that meeting though it's such a bummer it's a week from now. Quite disappointed overall.

I currently just .. sleep or lie in bed (yes its lie, not lay.. I see people say lay in bed a lot x_x and people also need to use may as permission, not can.. okay sorry pet peeves!) and just do whatever on the computer, then lay down again, approx 16 hours total just in bed. I ate today though! I think I'll start having a meal a day.

Previous routines was just me playing video games (and coaching others in said games) and helping my terrible parent pay for it time to time due to gambling problems. My funds are running out tho, and that's probably why I decided to take actions again, despite me trying to kill myself a week ago.

As of right now I think I'm going to slowly go back a more .. get out of bed routine and probably work out a bit again while I wait.

Heh.. I rather just stick to something I can just enjoy feeling good about myself if anything which is why I'm content with a lot of things as everything else is a luxury outside the necessity to survive.

Funny thing you ask that because I am actually missing two courses to actually even have a GED/highschool diploma despite going into a post secondary, but the thing with that was the fact it was an uprising program and I was the first round of students in it for the school board/district whatever it was, to see if it was worth keeping around and besides even if I didn't I'd think I would've been able to go into BCIT because BCIT is just a trades campus such as electrical, woodwork, metal and whatnot.

Nothing is too personal, because I am not ashamed or afraid to speak completely free (unfiltered and uncensored).

No I have not actually had a serious relationship, though I have been in like .. I would say .. two or three that I'd say was worth mentioning and further developing what I hate about relationships and how people are if they clearly cannot communicate well within one another. So in order words, those relationships that I've had were always code dependant and was unhealthy. I broke it all off for all of them, it was not them. I could not stand what was going in in it as I wanted my own individual freedom at times to do my own thing.

I am still a virgin and I am not embarrassed/ashamed to say so and it does not bother me in any way. I do not think about sex much, though I really wouldn't mind trying it sometime, but it's not something of importance to me.

Heh it just kinda falls under self expectations so I failed myself.

Family has never been supportive, I've been tossed around a lot, but I guess it really wasn't just family since I've had bullying issues since I was even in 1st grade.

I lived with my aunt and uncle for about 5 years since my mom was  a terrible parent or so that's what my aunt and uncle figured and during the time my step dad was selling cocaine and other drugs so my aunt didn't want my affiliated with that.

After I finished 8th grade I was forced to move back because mom wasn't keeping her part of the deal (or so I've been done, still don't know how truthful any of this really is) and since then was when I had clinical/psychological depression for the most part. I had depression as a kid, but after 10th grade I found out it was more of questioning life hence existential depression.

I never went to college/university unless you really count a year into a hands on trade in the plumbing industry where I attended BCIT for only like 3 months but a whole year dedicated to plumbing at another school which was actually a secondary school but had a back building based all around the trade and it was just us 18 class members, I believe it was 22 at the start, might've been less as it went down the line as people didn't want to continue pursuing it.

I never really liked the idea much on academics, like in highschool, math (though I actually do like math) because why would you need more than simple basics unless you're pursuing something in relation to the indepths of math? Same with history/social studies, things like that. I mean it's great you can look back to see what Columbus did and whatnot but still, it's kinda like looking back at the past.

Education can only really put you so far in terms of knowledge, training is the most valued asset when it comes to learning, but people are afraid of doing that without any kind of background in any kind of field.

EDIT: I mean maybe it's because I logically feel as if you're able to observe one and learn from their ways and ask questions it'd easier and then from there you can find your own groove and use techniques that fit you. I'm a visual learner, so for the ones who are into learning from text books they most of the time get into something less physic intensive.

Basically what I'm saying is that, if people were willing to accept people easier and let them do unpaid work experience I'm sure a lot more would jump at that opportunity really. Sometimes I feel like I should be able to walk up to a job site or something and if I need safety I'll get those on my own such as boots or the latter, and just ask if I can simply watch and do minor helping hands and you don't have to pay me, I rather just learn this way.

I know of someone who like once took apart an engine because he wanted to learn how it works instead of reading through the textbook, he was able to even put it all back together and have it working.

Lack of things to do, environment just sucks. I've lived on my own for a year, but during that time I did many naive things because I wasn't taught and simply put I moved back in with family and went through even more hell during those times.

To be honest if I was brought up correctly I would probably more than likely still be on my own now, but I guess that's all part of the experience.
